context.objective: Document how we carry out European Bank Account Administration, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.

The excerpt in “F03 FA-18A one page.pdf” describes confirming the request, entity and regional route, and says Compliance or Legal must confirm whether the Rule 4.1 notification path applies. Does that reflect how European bank-account requests are handled today?

Yes, that is how it starts. The Fund Administrator confirms whether it is a new account, a bank transition, a mandate change or a signatory refresh, confirms the legal entity and jurisdiction, identifies the regional review chain and records the business need and target timing. What the page does not show is what comes next. The Fund Administrator, with input from Fund Accounting and the client, assembles the bank package: the expected activity profile, the investor profile from approved KYC and AML sources, the economic purpose, the applicable regulatory thresholds, and the bank-specific forms, without changing approved facts. Then the Fund Administrator, Treasury and a regional reviewer confirm the KYC and CDD status against the regional Excel schedule, and prepare the bank mandate and signatory information. For a bank transition the mandate and signatories are refreshed, not reused without review. If there is a CDD block or a PEP concern we stop the setup and escalate it to Compliance and regional governance, and we do not go on until it is resolved and the decision is recorded.
Once the mandate and signatory information are prepared, what happens next in the account setup?

Next the complete package goes through the regional review chain: Administration, Fund Accounting, the Controller and the Head of Jurisdiction. Review comments are resolved, and the required regional approval has to be in place before anything is submitted. Then the package is submitted through the bank-approved channel and the submission record is kept. I do not know exactly who does the submitting, that is not defined. If a signatory or mandate mismatch is found, it is corrected before submission. After submission the bank may come back with queries. The Fund Administrator and the regional reviewers record the query in the query log, prepare the response from approved records only, never a speculative answer, and get regional or client approval if any facts changed or extra written confirmations are needed. Then we keep the response and decision record. If the bank has no queries we just wait for the bank confirmation.
Once the bank confirmation arrives, what marks the account setup as complete and what happens to the account next?

Once the bank confirms the opening or transition, Treasury or the Fund Administrator, the exact owner is not defined, confirms the account identity and status from the bank records, and checks that the mandate and signatories set up at the bank match the approved package. Then Treasury confirms the account is visible in Kyriba, when the account is in scope for Kyriba. If it is not visible, that is escalated, Treasury consolidated visibility is not marked complete, and we do not proceed to handoff until it is resolved and recorded. I do not know who the Treasury owner for that escalation is. After that the approved operational records are updated, without storing unredacted bank data outside authorized locations. The last step is done by the Fund Administrator or Treasury: store the approved package, mandate, signatory information, bank confirmation, review records and Kyriba records in the digital records binder, notify the authorized users in payment operations that the account is operational, and record any restrictions that are not yet resolved. It is finished when the records are stored and the handoff to Operations is complete. The exact notification list and the retention period are not defined, so I cannot tell you those.
What does this work enable for the fund or its operations once the account is handed off?
This capture still has open sections. 14 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.
